title: Runtime Stages, Capacity, Load, Alignment and Resilience
summary: Contemporary civilization contains systems in formation, expansion, saturation, pressure and reconfiguration at the same time, so a single rise-or-decline label is inadequate. Capacity and load examine remaining room, alignment asks whether systems support one another, and resilience and adaptability distinguish recovery from structural change.

blocks.text: Contemporary civilization contains systems in formation, expansion, saturation, pressure and reconfiguration at the same time, so a single rise-or-decline label is inadequate. Capacity and load examine remaining room, alignment asks whether systems support one another, and resilience and adaptability distinguish recovery from structural change.

These dimensions are not a civilization ranking. A society may have spare capacity in some layers and overload in others, or be resilient while adapting slowly. Assessment therefore has to preserve multiple layers and timescales.

This article provides structural observation rather than a ranking of civilizations. Future-capacity statements remain conditional; B6-WEB-B adds no live data and does not turn runtime readouts into outcome predictions.
